summary.text: A transformer is a passive component that passes electrical energy from one circuit to another through coils wound on a shared core.
A varying current in one coil makes a varying magnetic flux in the core, which induces a voltage in the other coils with no wire connecting them.
Step-up and step-down transformers change AC voltage levels, and they are essential to sending power over the grid.

facts.label: Voltage ratio
facts.value: Equals the ratio of turns in the windings

facts.label: Size range
facts.value: From under a cubic centimetre to hundreds of tons

facts.label: Based on
facts.value: Faraday's law of induction, discovered in 1831

items.prompt: A transformer's two coils are not electrically connected, yet power moves between them. How?

options.label: Through a hidden wire in the casing
Through a changing magnetic flux in the shared core
Through heat travelling along the core
Through static sparks between coils

items.explain: A varying current in one coil makes varying flux in the core, inducing an emf in the other coil without a conductive link.

items.prompt: A power company needs to lower the grid's AC voltage for houses. Which device does it use?

options.label: A step-down transformer
A step-up transformer
A DC battery
A magnet on a string

items.explain: Step-down transformers decrease voltage level and step-up ones increase it.

items.prompt: In an ideal transformer the secondary has twice as many turns as the primary. What does the secondary voltage do?

options.label: Halves
Stays equal
Doubles
Drops to zero

items.explain: The voltage ratio equals the turns ratio, since each winding sees the same flux.

items.prompt: A transformer is plugged into steady DC and no voltage appears at the output. Why?

options.label: The core is too heavy for DC
The wire is too thick for DC
The output coil is too hot for DC
The flux is steady, so nothing is induced

items.explain: Only a varying current makes varying flux that induces a voltage; transformers change AC voltage levels.

items.prompt: Some flux escapes the core and links only one winding. What is this called, and what does it cause?

options.label: Leakage flux, which worsens voltage regulation
Eddy flux, which melts the whole core
Ideal flux, which gives perfect coupling
Static flux, which has no effect on anything

items.explain: Flux that goes outside the windings is leakage flux, giving leakage inductance and inferior voltage regulation under heavy load.

items.prompt: Which feature is true of a real transformer but not an ideal one?

options.label: Voltage that follows the turns ratio
It loses energy to eddy currents in the core
It has two coils sharing one core
It works through changing flux

items.explain: The ideal model is lossless; real ones have unavoidable losses such as eddy current heating and leakage.
